title: The Orbit of the Rust Belt
premise: Marguerite Brightwater has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony network that stopped answering long ago. When the ship Perihelion returns from a failed deep-space jump with its crew mysteriously aged backward into children who remember their own deaths, Marguerite realizes the colony wasn't abandoned—it was erased, and the vault's seeds are the only record left of what humanity was. Racing a dying relay across dead space to broadcast the truth before the jump window closes, she must choose between saving the child-crew's chance to return home and exposing the corporate fleet that wrote them off. She sends the signal, stays behind as the vault's final caretaker, and dies content: the truth outlives her.
about_author: I. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent a decade documenting decommissioned research stations before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about people who keep promises no one asked them to make.

chapters.title: Seed Count, Day Four Thousand and One
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She performs her morning ritual in the vault—cataloguing seeds, logging weather, speaking aloud to an empty habitat ring. A routine transmission to the colony network returns static for the 400th consecutive day. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into habit; she almost prefers the silence.

chapters.title: The Thing That Falls Out of the Sky
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A burning shape crosses the sky and crashes in the salt flats—the Perihelion, a deep-jump vessel she thought was a legend. She finds the hatch open and small footprints leading away into the dust. Emotional beat: terror curdling into wonder; her first visitor in years.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Dying
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In a collapsed greenhouse she finds six crew members physically aged eight to twelve, including Captain Osei Vann, now a boy who recalls his own death in the jump. They recognize her name from fleet records—as a problem to be silenced. Emotional beat: dread beneath tenderness.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Vann's POV (the boy captain). He audits his own fragmented memories against the ship's black box, confirming the jump didn't fail—it succeeded, and something on the other side sent them back wrong. The fleet knew. Emotional beat: the horror of being believed by no one except a stranger.

chapters.title: What the Vault Is For
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She shows the children the seed archive: every crop, every extinct cultivar, a civilization in cold storage. Vann realizes the vault is the fleet's insurance policy—and why Marguerite was left alive. Emotional beat: belonging offered with strings attached.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. Ship telemetry shows one functioning relay in dead space can carry proof of the fleet's erasure order—but only during a jump-window alignment closing in nineteen days. The Perihelion can barely fly. Emotional beat: hope arriving as a deadline.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days of Small Repairs
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Montage of repair work: the children's small hands fit where adult hands couldn't; Marguerite teaches hydroponics as triage medicine. One child, Petra, refuses to help, insisting they should stay hidden. Emotional beat: fragile community forming under pressure.

chapters.title: A Signal From Someone Living
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The vault's ancient array catches a live transmission—a fleet salvage team inbound to strip the colony ruins and 'decontaminate anomalies.' Anomalies means them. Emotional beat: the safety of invisibility revoked.

chapters.title: Petra's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She calculates the odds: seven untrained people, a broken ship, nineteen days, versus a salvage cutter. Staying means capture; flying means probably dying. She lays out both funerals to the group. Emotional beat: bitter clarity from the youngest voice.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ensemble scene, Marguerite anchoring. By lamplight among the seed racks, they vote to fly. Vann confesses he remembers betraying his own crew in the original timeline—and asks them to override him if it happens again. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen, not owed.

chapters.title: Launch Window, Bad Weather
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. The Perihelion lifts through a salt storm, systems failing in sequence. Marguerite, who hasn't left Earth in eleven years, watches her whole world shrink to a blue smear. Emotional beat: grief and liberation indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Dead Space Is Not Empty
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the void between relays, the ship passes the jump scar where the crew died the first time. Instruments echo with their own death-signal. Petra begins to remember things that haven't happened yet. Emotional beat: time itself is untrustworthy.

chapters.title: The Salvage Cutter Finds Them
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. The fleet ship Meridian intercepts, hailing with Vann's own adult voice—a recorded loyalty test. Answering correctly buys hours; answering wrongly means boarding. Marguerite realizes the fleet always intended to retrieve the vault's location from her. Emotional beat: hunted by your own history.

chapters.title: Thirteen Days Left, No Fuel
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Adrift, they cannibalize the jump drive for reaction mass, guaranteeing they can never go home again. Petra, softening, gives Marguerite her ration. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed as investment in each other.

chapters.title: The Meridian's Mercy
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. The cutter offers sanctuary: return the children, forget the evidence, live comfortably. Vann remembers—in another loop he took this deal and it erased everyone anyway. He declines, and the cutter opens fire. Emotional beat: temptation answered with conviction.

chapters.title: Burn Toward the Edge
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A desperate slingshot around a dead gas giant, hull screaming, using the Meridian's own fire as thrust. The ship survives by seconds. Two children are injured; Marguerite uses seed-vault antibiotics meant for crops. Emotional beat: survival priced in what you burn behind you.

chapters.title: What Vann Remembers Next
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. His future-memories sharpen: he sees himself at the relay, sending the signal, and then nothing—which might mean peace or erasure. He tells Marguerite the truth about the first betrayal. She doesn't forgive him; she trusts him anyway. Emotional beat: trust as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Ensemble, climax begins. They dock with the derelict relay as the jump window opens. The Meridian arrives simultaneously. Vann and Marguerite split: she goes to the transmitter core, he draws the cutter's attention with the Perihelion. Emotional beat: every plan now costs someone everything.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, climax. Hand-splicing cables in vacuum, she uploads the erasure orders, the crew's testimony, and eleven years of vault logs to every colony band still listening. The Meridian locks weapons on the relay. Vann rams the Perihelion into its firing arc. Emotional beat: truth delivered at the cost of the messenger.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Signal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The blast wave; silence; then the relay's antenna catches responses—dozens of colonies, alive, receiving. The Meridian retreats, its crime now public. The children weep for a captain who isn't coming back. Emotional beat: victory that feels like a funeral.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Colony ships answer, offering passage. The children debate returning to a humanity that sold them once. Petra chooses to go—but leaves her journal with the relay, addressed to whoever comes next. Emotional beat: belonging redefined as something you carry.

chapters.title: Seed Count, Final Entry
chapters.summary: Marguerite's recorded log, posthumous frame. Back at the vault, older, she plants the first open-pollinated field as colony shuttles descend. Her last entry: the count of what survived. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—the price was paid, the harvest belongs to everyone.
